## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

Trail: feat: user-global settings tier + hook gates (global enable: core)
  Number:  1012
  ID:      01M07MZT749ESGGDMHW8E2XJM0
  Branch:  feat/global-core
  Base:    main
  Status:  open
  Author:  peyton-alt
  Phase:   building
  URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1012
  Assignees: peyton-alt
  Type:      task
  Created: 2026-08-11T19:48:32Z
  Updated: 2026-08-19T00:38:11Z

Description:
Problem:
Entire requires per-repository setup (.entire/settings.json) to track agent sessions. Users managing multiple repos with Entire wanted a way to enable tracking globally across all their repos without configuring each one individually.
Solution:
Added a user-global settings tier in ~/.config/entire/settings.json that auto-enables Entire in any repository without repo-level setup. The feature includes:
Global config structure with enabled flag and two exclude lists:
exclude_paths: doublestar globs (with ~ expansion) to skip specific directories
exclude_origins: doublestar globs matching normalized host/owner/repo origins to exclude repos from specific sources
New gitremote.GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet() helper to look up all configured URLs for a remote, distinguishing between "not configured" and lookup errors — used to check whether a repo's origin matches an exclusion pattern.
Core predicate IsActiveForRepo() that hooks now use instead of IsSetUpAndEnabled(). It checks repo-level setup first (making explicit repo-level disable veto global mode), then falls back to global-mode activation if the repo has no setup.
Comprehensive exclusion matching with case-insensitive path folding on macOS/Windows (where filesystems are case-insensitive), and case-insensitive origin matching. Invalid exclude patterns are skipped so one bad entry doesn't break the list.
Fail-closed safety: all errors during global-mode checks (unreadable settings, missing worktree root, origin lookup failure) disable global mode to prevent silent misbehavior.
Hook entry points now consult the global tier at both gates (registry dispatch and git-command initialization), ensuring global repos get session logging and redaction like repo-level setups do.

+// GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet returns every raw URL stored for the named git
+// remote in dir, distinguishing "remote not configured" from a failed lookup:
+// exit code 1 from `git config --get-all` is reported as found=false with a
+// nil error — for well-formed remote names that means the key is unset (git
+// also exits 1 for invalid key names). Because that fallback also fires when
+// dir is not a repository at all (the lookup then reads global/system scope),
+// exit 1 is trusted only after verifying dir is inside a repo; a non-repo dir
+// returns an error. found=true means the key EXISTS: stored values are
+// returned verbatim (whitespace-trimmed), including blank ones, so a caller
+// can fail closed on an uncheckable `url =` entry. Any other failure (dir
+// missing, git unavailable, context canceled) returns an error. `git remote get-url`
+// could make the same distinction — its failures are distinguishable too
+// (exit 2 for "no such remote" vs 128 for not-a-repo) — but
+// it is deliberately not used, for two reasons: (i) it expands
+// url.<base>.insteadOf rewrites, which would break the ExcludeOrigins
+// contract that patterns match what git config STORES
+// (settings.GlobalConfig.ExcludeOrigins — a stored gh:acme/widgets must not
+// come back as git@github.com:acme/widgets), and (ii) `git config
+// --get-all` gives the clean exit-1-means-unset contract this function's

+// match on ANY of them as a match.

+// builds a repo's remotes from the full config stack, so a remote defined in
+// global/system scope IS that repo's origin (git remote -v lists it and
+// fetch uses it). Scoping to --local would make origin exclusion diverge
+// from git's own view, treating such a repo as origin-less.
+func GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet(ctx context.Context, dir, remoteName string) (urls []string, found bool, err error) {
+	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "config", "--get-all", "remote."+remoteName+".url")
+	if dir != "" {
+		cmd.Dir = dir
+	}
+	output, err := cmd.Output()
+	if err != nil {
+		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
+		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 {
+			// Exit 1 means "key unset" only inside a repository: outside one,
+			// git config silently falls back to global/system scope and exits 1
+			// for absent-there too, which would misreport "not a repo" as "no

+			inRepo := isGitRepoDir(ctx, dir)
+			// Checked after the probe regardless of its outcome: cancellation
+			// can fail the probe (report it, not a bogus "not a repo") or land
+			// after the probe already succeeded (don't swallow it into a clean
+			// "no origin configured").
+			if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
+				return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("looking up remote %q: %w", remoteName, ctxErr)
+			}
+			if !inRepo {
+				return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("looking up remote %q: not a git repository", remoteName)
+			}
+			return nil, false, nil
+		}
+		return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("looking up remote %q: %w", remoteName, err)

content.text:
All 13 findings on trail #1012 are resolved, so I re-reviewed the branch from scratch. First, verification that Monday's three fixes hold end-to-end through a real binary (not just unit tests) — probe repos + a temp `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, using `.entire/` creation as the activity signal:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `https://github.com/acme/widgets/` vs `exclude_origins: [github.com/acme/widgets]` | excluded ✓ |
| `git@github.com:acme/widgets.GIT` | excluded ✓ |
| `…/widgets.git/` vs `github.com/acme/*` | excluded ✓ |
| `exclude_origins: ["["]`, repo with **no** origin | fail-closed ✓ |
| `remote.origin.url=` (blank value) | fail-closed ✓ |
| unknown key in settings.json | fail-closed ✓ |
| no-origin repo, `github.com/**` | active (as documented) ✓ |
| `exclude_paths_exact` parent vs nested repo | parent inactive, nested active ✓ |

`mise run lint` clean; settings + gitremote suites and all six new gate tests pass.

Five new findings.

**1 — medium: global mode writes an *unignored* log into repos the user never set up; the next `git add -A` commits it.**
`initHookLogging` (`cmd/entire/cli/hooks_git_cmd.go:136`) now passes for global-tier repos and calls `logging.Init`, creating `.entire/logs/entire.log`. Nothing on the git-hook path calls `strategy.EnsureEntireGitignore` — that lives in `strategy.EnsureSetup`, reached only from the agent TurnStart handler (`lifecycle.go:604`) and `entire enable`. Under repo-level setup the ignore file always predates the first hook; under global mode a plain `git commit` in a repo where no agent turn has happened yet does not.

Verified: fresh repo, global on, `entire hooks git post-commit` → `?? .entire/`, and `git add -An .` prints `add '.entire/logs/entire.log'`.

Fix is one line: call `strategy.EnsureEntireGitignore(ctx)` in `initHookLogging` before `logging.Init`. It's idempotent, and it's safe against the status-cache rule in CLAUDE.md — `initHookLogging` runs in `PersistentPreRunE`, before the dispatcher installs a cache. Separately: after the agent path *does* run, `.entire/.gitignore` itself stays untracked, so `?? .entire/` persists in a repo the user never opted into. Repo-level mode intends that file to be committed; global mode has no such consent, so that's worth a deliberate call.

**2 — medium: bare `entire` in a globally-active repo runs the enable wizard and silently converts the repo off the global tier.**
`root.go:98` still gates on `!settings.IsSetUpAny(ctx)`. Verified: in a global-mode repo, bare `entire` printed `✓ Configured project / .entire/settings.json`. From then on `IsActiveForRepo` takes the repo-level branch permanently, so adding that repo to `exclude_paths`/`exclude_origins` afterwards has **no effect** — the user has to edit the repo's own settings.json. Gate that flow on the global tier too, or tell the user what enabling will pin. Related and presumably split D: `entire status` prints `○ not set up (run 'entire enable' to get started)` in a repo hooks are actively tracking — `global.go`'s comment promises status/doctor as the diagnosability story; worth confirming D covers this exact string, since it's the first thing users hit.

**3 — low: `IsSetUpAndEnabled` is now dead in production, and its regression test guards the unused function.**
All three gates moved to `IsActiveForRepo`; zero non-test callers remain. The bug it was written for (settings.local.json-only repos activating hooks, `settings/settings_test.go:1375-1397`) now lives in `IsActiveForRepo`, whose tests cover only the local-only `{"enabled":false}` veto, not the positive local-only case. Delete it and re-point the test, or keep it and add the positive case.

**4 — low: `splitOwnerRepo` isn't idempotent for `…/repo/.git` — same fail-open shape as Monday's high finding.**
`strings.TrimRight(path, "/")` runs *before* the `.git` strip (`gitremote.go:322-331`), so:

```
https://github.com/acme/widgets/.git  -> owner="acme" repo="widgets/"
ssh://git@host/srv/widgets/.git       -> repo="widgets/"
```

`normalizeOrigin` then returns a non-empty `host/acme/widgets/`, which misses the fail-closed empty branch and matches neither `…/widgets` nor `…/*`. Rare URL shape, one-line fix (trim trailing slashes again after the `.git` strip), plus a row next to the existing `.git/` case.

**5 — low, perf: with `exclude_origins` set, every hook process forks the origin lookup twice.**
Measured with a `git` shim on PATH: post-commit = 2× `config --get-all remote.origin.url`; agent TurnStart = 2×. Both gates call `IsActiveForRepo` independently and `GlobalModeActive` isn't memoized, unlike `paths.WorktreeRoot`, which caches per process. With no exclude lists configured: 0 extra forks, so the `182372f73` ordering invariant does hold. Memoizing `GlobalModeActive` per process fixes it — its own doc comment already anticipates that, including keeping the settings-read-before-fork order.

Nit: `matchesExcludePathExactFold` (`global.go`) lowercases `v` inside the inner root loop, mutating the outer loop variable each iteration — idempotent today, so harmless; hoist it like `matchesExcludePathFold` does.

One design note, not a finding: `push_sessions` defaults on, so enabling the global tier means `git push` carries checkpoint transcripts to every repo's origin — including repos the user doesn't own. The dotfiles finding settled the *mechanism* (opt-out via `exclude_paths_exact`); what's left is discoverability, since consent is now machine-wide rather than per repo.

Want me to file 1–5 as trail findings on #1012, or start with the fix for #1?

content.text:
One new finding this pass, and it's the most serious so far — `01M0DX240HT6` (High), `strategy/common.go:110`.

**Global mode modifies tracked files in repos the user never set up.** `EnsureSetup` → `InstallGitHook` resolves its target via `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which honors `core.hooksPath`. When that points into the worktree — the widespread `.githooks` convention, or husky ≤ v8 where `.husky` is tracked — Entire renames the user's hooks to `*.pre-entire` and writes chaining wrappers over tracked paths. Verified with a tracked `.husky` + `core.hooksPath=.husky`: one agent TurnStart in a repo with no `.entire/` produced

```
 M .husky/commit-msg
 M .husky/pre-push
?? .husky/commit-msg.pre-entire  ?? .husky/pre-push.pre-entire
?? .husky/post-commit  ?? .husky/post-rewrite  ?? .husky/prepare-commit-msg
```

The "Backed up existing…" notices go to hook stderr, which nobody reads, and the next `git add -A` publishes those wrappers to a shared repo. Hook behavior is preserved (the wrappers chain to the backups), so this is about unsolicited changes to tracked files rather than breakage. With `core.hooksPath` unset it all lands in `.git/hooks` and is invisible to git — that's why this specific configuration is the sharp edge, and nothing in the codebase detects it (only the `ENOTDIR` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` check).

Two things I checked this pass that came back **clean**, so no findings:

- **Pre-push doesn't break pushes.** I expected global mode to risk aborting `git push` when a forge rejects `entire/checkpoints/v1`. It doesn't: `prePush` only returns errors for privacy-critical OPF failures (`hooks_git_cmd.go:334-350`), so a rejected checkpoint push leaves the user's push alone.
- **The test files are solid.** 644 lines of `global_test.go` plus the darwin fold test: every fail-closed leg has a subtest with a stated rationale, `t.Chdir`/`t.Setenv` correctly preclude `t.Parallel`, remote fixtures use `testutil.GitIsolatedEnv`, and the unreadable-file branch is exercised portably (directory-at-settings.json). `go.mod`/`go.sum` add only `doublestar/v4 v4.9.1`, already the repo's glob library.

Trail #1012 now has six open findings: 1 high, 2 medium, 3 low.

package strategy

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/testutil"
)

// Concurrent first-install probe: N processes/goroutines entering
// InstallGitHook at once on a repo that has a pre-existing user hook.
func TestZZRaceProbe(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)
	hooksDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "hooks")
	userHook := "#!/bin/sh\necho USER_HOOK_RAN\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(hooksDir, "commit-msg"), []byte(userHook), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Chdir(dir)

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			_, _ = InstallGitHook(t.Context(), true, false, false)
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()

	final, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(hooksDir, "commit-msg"))
	backup, berr := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(hooksDir, "commit-msg.pre-entire"))
	chained := strings.Contains(string(final), "commit-msg.pre-entire")
	backupIsUserHook := berr == nil && string(backup) == userHook
	backupIsEntireWrapper := berr == nil && strings.Contains(string(backup), "Entire CLI hooks")

	t.Logf("final-chains-to-backup=%v backup-is-user-hook=%v backup-is-entire-wrapper=%v", chained, backupIsUserHook, backupIsEntireWrapper)
	switch {
	case backupIsEntireWrapper:
		t.Errorf("LOST: user hook destroyed; backup holds Entire's own wrapper (recursive chain)")
	case backupIsUserHook && !chained:
		t.Errorf("ORPHANED: user hook preserved in backup but final hook does not chain to it — user hook never runs again")
	case !backupIsUserHook:
		t.Errorf("MISSING BACKUP: user hook not preserved (err=%v)", berr)
	}
}
EOF
go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/ -run TestZZRaceProbe -count=12 2>&1 | grep -E 'final-chains|LOST|ORPHANED|MISSING|^ok|^FAIL|^---' | head -30

content.text:
One new finding, and it's the worst one yet — `01M0F2AC7226` (High), `strategy/hooks.go:325-343`.

**Concurrent first-install destroys a pre-existing user hook and leaves the installed hook chaining to itself.** This branch moves first-ever hook installation out of `entire enable` (serial, once) and into `EnsureSetup` on TurnStart, which runs inside hook processes that can be concurrent. The backup step is an unsynchronized read → rename → write with no file lock:

- A renames the user's hook to `*.pre-entire`, writes its wrapper.
- B, holding a read from before that rename, renames the **wrapper** onto the same backup path — `rename(2)` overwrites — destroying the user's hook, then writes a chained wrapper.

Verified two ways on a repo with a pre-existing `commit-msg`:

| probe | bad outcome |
|---|---|
| 8 concurrent in-process `InstallGitHook` calls | 5 / 12 runs |
| 8 parallel real `entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit`, global mode, no `.entire/` | 2 / 5 rounds |

In the bad rounds `commit-msg.pre-entire` contains Entire's own wrapper, the user's hook text is gone from *both* files, and the backup's chain line points at `commit-msg.pre-entire` — itself. So every subsequent `git commit` re-executes the same script until it hits a process or CPU limit. I did not run it.

Repo-level setup isn't exposed at first install: `enable` installs before any hook runs, so `EnsureSetup` always finds `IsGitHookInstalled` true and skips. The exposed population is repos with pre-existing hooks — the same set as yesterday's tracked-`core.hooksPath` finding, which is why these two want fixing together.

Trail #1012: **7 open findings** — 2 high, 2 medium, 3 low. Both highs are about what the gate unlocks in repos that never opted in, rather than the tier's own logic, which has now held up under three passes.

  -m 'On Windows a Unix-style rooted exclude pattern is accepted but can never match — fail open, and the mirror-image mistake fails closed on Unix.

The guard rejects a pattern only when BOTH tests fail: `!strings.HasPrefix(slashed, "/") && !filepath.IsAbs(pattern)`. On Windows `/code/**` satisfies the HasPrefix leg, so it is accepted even though filepath.IsAbs is false for it, and it can never match a root like `C:/code/repo` — the exclusion silently does not apply and the repo is tracked.

Asymmetry, verified on darwin: the mirror mistake `C:/code/**` returns `exclude_paths[0]: relative pattern cannot match an absolute worktree root`, i.e. fail closed. So one shared ~/.config/entire/settings.json across machines fails safe on Unix and open on Windows — exactly the direction the tier is designed to avoid. Windows half is reasoned from filepath.Clean/IsAbs semantics, not executed (no Windows host here).

Adjacent to 7aaeceb70, which pins the drive-letter case that DOES work. Fix: on Windows require a volume name (filepath.VolumeName != "" or IsAbs) rather than accepting a leading slash. A regression test needs "Windows" in its top-level name to be selected by the ci.yml test-windows job (`go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... -run "(Windows|MSYS)"`), the same convention 7aaeceb70 follows.' 2>&1 | tail -3
entire trail finding add --severity low --confidence 0.8 \
  --file cmd/entire/cli/root.go --line 103 \
  --client-id review-globalcore-unusable-tier-reads-as-no \
  -m 'The new bare-entire gate treats "global tier unusable" as "tier says no", and nothing tells the user their global config is broken.

GlobalModeActive is fail-closed by design: every error path returns false. At the gates that is correct. At this call site the consequence inverts — false means "run the setup flow", which writes .entire/settings.json and permanently pins the repo out of the global tier (the harm 9daa4e6c0 set out to prevent).

Verified with the rebuilt binary: ~/.config/entire/settings.json = {"global":{"enabled":true},"typo":1} (strict decoding rejects the unknown key) -> bare `entire` ran the full setup flow and wrote .entire/settings.json. The user gets no hint that their global file is unusable: the Debug log in GlobalModeActive is dropped because logging.Init has not run, and `entire status` prints "not set up" either way.

Fix: distinguish "tier unusable" from "tier says no" at this call site (e.g. have the predicate return an explicit reason), and surface the unusable-config case in status/doctor — the diagnosability work global.go already defers to a later split.' 2>&1 | tail -3

Finding:   01M0DX240HT6Y42Y7NTGFX2FSQ
Status:    resolved
Freshness: current
Severity:  high
Confidence: 0.90
Location: cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:110

Global mode modifies TRACKED files in repos the user never set up, when core.hooksPath points into the worktree.

The gate now reaches strategy.EnsureSetup on TurnStart (lifecycle.go:604) in repos with no repo-level setup, and EnsureSetup installs git hooks (common.go:110). GetHooksDir resolves through `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which honors core.hooksPath — so for the common `.githooks` convention (and husky <= v8, whose .husky is tracked) the hooks dir is a tracked directory, and InstallGitHook renames the user hooks to *.pre-entire and writes chaining wrappers over tracked paths.

Verified: repo with tracked .husky/{pre-commit,commit-msg,pre-push} + core.hooksPath=.husky, global on, no .entire; one agent TurnStart produced
  M .husky/commit-msg
  M .husky/pre-push
  ?? .husky/commit-msg.pre-entire, .husky/pre-push.pre-entire, .husky/post-commit, .husky/post-rewrite, .husky/prepare-commit-msg
The "Backed up existing ..." notices go to hook stderr, which the user normally never sees, and the next `git add -A` publishes Entire wrappers to a shared repo. Hook behavior itself is preserved (wrappers chain to the backups) — the defect is unsolicited tracked-file changes.

With core.hooksPath unset (.git/hooks) nothing lands in the worktree, so the tracked-hooksPath case is the sharp edge, and nothing detects it today (only the ENOTDIR/core.hooksPath=/dev/null check in InstallGitHook). Options: deactivate global mode when the resolved hooks dir is inside the worktree (fail closed, consistent with the tier), install only into a hooks dir under the git dir, or require repo-level opt-in for those repos.

content.content:
===== 01M0DX240HT6 high resolved
Superseded upstack by split B, which replaces this exact call path: on feat/global-invisible, lifecycle.go's TurnStart calls strategy.EnsureSetupForHook (not EnsureSetup), which routes every repo WITHOUT repo-level setup through MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup (global_setup.go:206-208) — a lazy setup that by contract never creates a worktree file, and whose HooksDirIsWorktreeResident guard (global_setup.go:64-82) detects exactly this finding's sharp edge: core.hooksPath resolving inside the worktree (committed .husky / .githooks) skips git-hook installation entirely, so no tracked file is ever renamed or wrapped. The guard is symlink-robust (resolveExistingPrefix on both sides) and fails toward skip on resolve errors. The chosen remedy is the finding's first option refined: not deactivating the whole tier but skipping only the git-hook leg — agent-side session capture still works, and split D's doctor names the state ("GIT HOOKS SKIPPED (core.hooksPath inside the worktree)") with repo-level enable as the explicit opt-in for git-hook capture, pinned by TestCheckGlobalTracking_ExplainsWorktreeResidentHooksPath. Repos WITH repo-level setup keep today's install-into-configured-hooksPath behavior — that path is user-opted-in. Exposure is limited to the window where A has landed and B has not, within the one release train the stack ships in (same caveat as the unignored-log and double-fork findings resolved earlier on this trail). EMPIRICALLY REPRODUCED against a binary built from feat/global-invisible tip: the finding's exact scenario (tracked .husky/{pre-commit,commit-msg,pre-push}, core.hooksPath=.husky, global on, no .entire) with BOTH hook routes exercised (entire hooks git post-commit + entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit, exit 0 each). Result: git status --porcelain EMPTY — no M .husky/*, no *.pre-entire backups, no Entire wrappers, hook scripts byte-identical. Non-vacuous: the run set global_setup_completed=true in .git/entire/preferences.json (the guard branch ran and skipped install) and created the session state (phase active) — global tracking fully engaged while the worktree stayed untouched, versus the M/?? entries the same repro produces on A.

===== 01M0DVV2N4VS high resolved
Verified NOT a bug — the guard already contains the suggested fix: line 167 is a conjunction, `!strings.HasPrefix(slashed, "/") && !filepath.IsAbs(pattern)`, and on Windows filepath.IsAbs("C:/code/**") is true (drive letter + separator), so the second conjunct accepts drive-letter absolutes and the rejection branch never fires for them; filepath.Clean+ToSlash preserve the C:/ form for the doublestar match against the ToSlash-ed worktree root, with the existing Windows/darwin case folding. A C:/-style pattern IS rejected on non-Windows machines, where it is genuinely not absolute — correct, and moot since the settings file is per-machine. Pinned in 7aaeceb70 (feat/global-core) by TestMatchesExcludePath_WindowsDriveAbsolute, which runs on the ci.yml test-windows leg (gated on filepath.IsAbs('C:/code') so the gate is the property under test), plus a GOOS=windows go vet pass locally.

===== 01M0DEPYQY2J medium resolved
Superseded upstack by split B's entire charter: .entire/logs is one of B's runtimeDataPrefixes, so for globally-tracked repos logging.Init resolves through the invisible routing into <git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/<key>/logs — no worktree file exists for git add to pick up, and git status stays byte-clean (B's core invariant, pinned by its routing tests). The suggested fix — writing .entire/.gitignore from initHookLogging — would itself violate that invariant by creating a visible worktree artifact in repos the user never opted into, which also answers the finding's separate "?? .entire/ persists" question: under B nothing appears in the worktree at all. Exposure is limited to the window where A has landed and B has not, within one release train.

entire trail finding update 01M0F2AC7226 --confidence 0.98 -m 'Concurrent first-install destroys a pre-existing user hook and leaves the installed hook chaining to itself. SURVIVES SPLIT B — re-verified against its tip.

Mechanism: first-ever hook installation moves out of `entire enable` (serial, once) into hook processes that can run concurrently. The backup step is an unsynchronized read -> rename -> write with no file lock. A renames the user hook to *.pre-entire and writes its wrapper; B, holding a read from before that rename, renames the *wrapper* onto the same backup path (rename(2) overwrites), destroying the user hook, then writes a chained wrapper. Result: commit-msg.pre-entire whose own chain line points at commit-msg.pre-entire, so every later `git commit` re-executes the same script until a process/CPU limit. Not executed, for obvious reasons.

On A (feat/global-core, EnsureSetup at lifecycle.go:604 -> common.go:110):
- 8 concurrent in-process InstallGitHook calls: 5/12 runs lost the hook.
- 8 parallel real `entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit` processes, global mode, no .entire: 2/5 rounds.

On B (feat/global-invisible tip, binary built from it), same repro with a pre-existing .git/hooks/commit-msg: 3/6 rounds lost the hook, backup self-references twice, while `git status --porcelain` stayed EMPTY — B invisible-routing invariant holds, the race is orthogonal to it. B does not fix this because MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup (global_setup.go) reads prefs.GlobalSetupCompleted at entry and writes it only at the end (line 118), with `if !IsGitHookInstalled(ctx) { ... installGitHooks(...) }` in between and no lock anywhere in the file — so two concurrent hook processes both observe "not done" and both install. B hooks.go keeps the identical os.Rename backup logic. HooksDirIsWorktreeResident does not help: it only skips the install when core.hooksPath is inside the worktree, and this repro is the plain .git/hooks case.

Exposed population: globally-tracked repos with a pre-existing non-Entire hook in .git/hooks (pre-commit framework, lint-staged, hand-written hooks) where two agent turns start concurrently — not limited to the A-without-B window.

Fix: serialize the install (the clone-preferences lock B already has, or an O_EXCL sentinel spanning read-install-write), and make the backup rename fail rather than overwrite (link(2), or re-read under the lock and skip when the source already carries entireHookMarker).' 2>&1 | tail -3

That finding asked about `C:/code/**` and was correctly closed: the guard is a conjunction, `!strings.HasPrefix(slashed, "/") && !filepath.IsAbs(pattern)`, and filepath.IsAbs is true for drive-letter paths, so they are accepted (pinned by 7aaeceb70). So the identical class of user error fails safe on Unix and open on Windows, the direction the tier is designed to avoid. Windows half is reasoned from filepath.Clean/IsAbs semantics, not executed (no Windows host here).

Fix: require a volume name on Windows (filepath.VolumeName != "" , or just drop the HasPrefix leg and rely on filepath.IsAbs, which is correct on both platforms). content.text:
Yes — Peyton pushed two commits (`9daa4e6c0`, `7aaeceb70`), and separately, several of my findings were resolved by someone else while I was away. I fast-forwarded the local branch (clean tree, pure ff) and checked all of it.

**Peyton's two commits, verified fixed:**
- `root.go` now also requires `!settings.GlobalModeActive(ctx)`. Rebuilt binary: global-active repo → help, no `.entire/settings.json` written; globally *excluded* repo → setup flow still offered, which is the right call. Resolved `01M0DEQDFNYZ`.
- `splitOwnerRepo` gained a second `TrimRight` after the `.git` strip — same effect as my patch. `…/repo/.git` and `git@…:acme/repo/.git` both yield `repo`. Resolved `01M0DERYRXM2`.
- Bonus: a `TestMatchesExcludePath_WindowsDriveAbsolute` that correctly follows the `ci.yml` `-run '(Windows|MSYS)'` naming convention, so it actually runs on the Windows leg. Lint and all touched suites green on `7aaeceb70`.

**Resolutions by others — I checked the claims rather than trusting them, and all three hold:**
- Tracked `core.hooksPath` (my high) → split B's `HooksDirIsWorktreeResident` guard genuinely skips the git-hook leg; `EnsureSetupForHook` exists in 5 files on that branch.
- Unignored `.entire/logs` (my medium) → B routes logs out of the worktree. My own B-tip probe corroborates it independently: `git status --porcelain` stayed empty. Their rebuttal that my suggested fix (writing `.entire/.gitignore`) would itself violate B's invariant is correct — that suggestion was wrong for the upstack design.
- Double origin fork → the `globalModeCached` memo does exist in `settings/global.go` on the later splits.

**One correction to a resolution.** My race finding was *not* superseded by B, so I re-verified against a binary built from B's tip and updated the finding with that evidence. Same repro, plain `.git/hooks/commit-msg`: **3/6 rounds lost the user's hook**, backup self-referencing, while B's worktree stayed byte-clean — the race is orthogonal to B's invariant. B doesn't fix it because `MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup` reads `prefs.GlobalSetupCompleted` at entry and writes it only at the end, with the install in between and no lock in the file; `HooksDirIsWorktreeResident` only covers the worktree-resident case. So exposure isn't limited to the "A landed, B hasn't" window.

**Two new low findings from this pass:**
- `01M0F2KND0MT` — the same conjunction at `global.go:167` that correctly *accepts* `C:/code/**` also accepts `/c/code/**`, which can never match on Windows → silent fail-open. Distinct from `01M0DVV2N4VS`, which was rightly dismissed; and "the settings file is per-machine" doesn't cover it, since `/c/code` is the native MSYS spelling. The mirror mistake fails *closed* on Unix — verified on darwin.
- `01M0F2KQ3YPD` — the new bare-`entire` gate reads "global tier unusable" as "tier says no". With an unknown key in `~/.config/entire/settings.json`, bare `entire` ran full setup and pinned the repo; nothing tells the user their global config is broken.

Open now: 1 high, 2 low.

`01M0F2AC7226` — the concurrent first-install race, at `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks.go:325-343`.

Two hook processes install git hooks at the same time on a repo that has a pre-existing non-Entire hook. The backup step is an unsynchronized read → rename → write with no lock: A renames the user's hook to `commit-msg.pre-entire` and writes its wrapper; B, holding a read from before that rename, renames the *wrapper* onto the same backup path (`rename(2)` overwrites). The user's hook is gone from both files, and the installed hook now chains to a copy of itself, so every later `git commit` re-executes the same script until it hits a process or CPU limit.

Evidence: 5/12 runs with 8 concurrent in-process installs; 2/5 rounds with 8 parallel real `entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit` processes on this branch; 3/6 rounds against a binary built from split B's tip.

It's the one finding not covered upstack — B's `HooksDirIsWorktreeResident` only skips the install when `core.hooksPath` is inside the worktree, and this is the plain `.git/hooks` case. `MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup` reads its "already done" marker at entry and writes it at the end with the install in between and no lock, so both processes see "not done".

Fix is two-part: serialize the install (B already has a clone-preferences lock to reuse, or an `O_EXCL` sentinel spanning read-install-write), and make the backup rename refuse to overwrite — `link(2)`, or re-read under the lock and skip when the source already carries `entireHookMarker`.

15	// TestInstallGitHook_ConcurrentInstallPreservesUserHook pins that two hook
16	// processes entering the install at the same moment cannot lose a pre-existing
17	// user hook.
18	//
19	// The backup step is a read -> rename -> write with no lock across it. A reads
20	// the user hook, renames it to <hook>.pre-entire and writes its wrapper; B,
21	// still holding a read from before that rename, sees no marker and no backup
22	// and renames the path again — but by then the path holds A's wrapper, and
23	// rename(2) overwrites the destination. The user hook is then gone from both
24	// files and the installed hook chains to a copy of itself, so every later git
25	// operation on that hook re-executes it until a process or CPU limit.
26	//
27	// Two assertions per hook cover both losing interleavings: the backup must
28	// still be the user's script (not an Entire wrapper), and the installed hook
29	// must chain to that backup — otherwise the user's hook is orphaned and
30	// silently never runs again.
31	//
32	// Every hook spec is seeded, so each round gets one independent chance to
33	// interleave per spec. Detection is still probabilistic per round, so the
34	// round count is sized to fail even on a single-CPU runner (measured: ~5% of rounds interleave at GOMAXPROCS=1, ~25% at 2, ~60% at 4, under -race). A correct
35	// implementation cannot corrupt, so the test is stable once this is fixed.
36	//
37	// No t.Parallel: t.Chdir plus the package-level hooks-dir and worktree-root
38	// caches are process-global.

41			rounds     = 120
42			installers = 4
43		)
44

52		}
53		userHook := func(name string) string {
54			return fmt.Sprintf("#!/bin/sh\necho USER_HOOK_%s\n", name)
55		}
56	
57		corrupted := 0
58		for round := range rounds {
59			dir := t.TempDir()
60			testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)
61	
62			hooksDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "hooks")
63			if err := os.MkdirAll(hooksDir, 0o755); err != nil {
64				t.Fatalf("round %d: create hooks dir: %v", round, err)
65			}
66			for _, spec := range specs {
67				if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(hooksDir, spec.name), []byte(userHook(spec.name)), 0o755); err != nil {

110				}

The failing test is written, RED, and lint-clean. The trail update didn't land, though — see the note at the end.

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks_concurrent_install_test.go`** (uncommitted, one new file, nothing else touched):

`TestInstallGitHook_ConcurrentInstallPreservesUserHook` seeds a user script for **every** `buildHookSpecs` entry (derived from the production helper, so it can't drift), runs 4 concurrent `InstallGitHook` calls per round across 120 rounds, and asserts per hook that (a) the backup still holds the user's script rather than an Entire wrapper, and (b) the installed hook chains to that backup — the two assertions cover both losing interleavings, destruction and orphaning.

Currently: `--- FAIL`, 235 corrupt-hook reports, ~2s. Fails 3/3 runs at `GOMAXPROCS=1` and `2` under `-race`, so it won't go quiet on a small CI runner. I got there by measurement, not guesswork: 8 installers on one hook only reproduced 2/24 rounds, and *more* goroutines made it rarer; seeding all five specs at 4 installers is what made it near-deterministic (measured per-round rates ~5% at 1 CPU, ~25% at 2, ~60% at 4).

**A correction to the fix I gave you.** I verified the test can go green, and my earlier `link(2)` suggestion is wrong — it makes things worse. `os.Link` + `os.Remove` leaves a window where the hook and its backup share one inode, and `writeHookFile`'s in-place `O_TRUNC` then reaches through into the backup: every round corrupted, all five hooks, versus ~60% before. What actually works is backing the hook up as a **copy** created with `O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_EXCL` (the bytes are already in hand from the `existing` read, and `EEXIST` means another installer got there first, so its backup is left intact), plus re-deriving `backupExists` via `fileExists(backupPath)` right before choosing chained-vs-plain content. With that patch the new test passes 3/3 at `GOMAXPROCS=2` and `4` under `-race`, and the whole `strategy` suite is green (42s). I reverted the fix so the test stays RED — the diff is at `scratchpad/candidate-fix.diff` if you want it.

Two things to flag:

- The test will make CI red until the fix lands. It's uncommitted, so that's your call on timing.
- **I could not update the finding on the trail.** All `entire trail finding` calls — including reads — now return `trail API: API error: invalid trail_id (status 400)`, for trail 1012 by branch, number, and ULID, and for an unrelated trail (1110) too. They worked earlier in this session; `entire trail show` and `entire trail list` still work, so it's scoped to the findings endpoints. Looks like a server-side regression in the last half hour rather than anything about my calls. The finding still carries the pre-correction text saying `link(2)` — worth fixing once the API recovers, since following it as written would make the bug worse. Want me to retry in a bit?

commit d676f4614fbac40646514a19e020db26a8c59f9e
Author: Peyton Montei <peyton@entire.io>
Date:   Thu Aug 20 10:07:28 2026 -0700

    fix(global): serialize hook install/remove; harden the bare-entire and exclude guards
    
    Trail 1012 findings:
    
    - Concurrent first-install race (HIGH): global mode moves first-ever git
      hook installation into hook processes that fire concurrently, and the
      unsynchronized read→rename→write could rename a half-installed wrapper
      over the user's hook backup — destroying the hook and leaving a
      wrapper chaining to itself. InstallGitHook and RemoveGitHook now take
      a cross-process flock in the git common dir (never the hooks dir,
      which can be worktree-resident). Regression test mutation-verified:
      fails on the unlocked code with the exact self-chain corruption.
    - Bare 'entire' no longer treats an UNUSABLE global config as "tier says
      no": the gate reads the enabled bit itself — an unreadable settings
      file gets a stderr warning instead of a wizard that would pin the repo
      out of the tier, and a tier-enabled-but-excluded repo is not funneled

content.content:
fix(global): serialize hook install/remove; harden the bare-entire and exclude guards

Trail 1012 findings:

- Concurrent first-install race (HIGH): global mode moves first-ever git
  hook installation into hook processes that fire concurrently, and the
  unsynchronized read→rename→write could rename a half-installed wrapper
  over the user's hook backup — destroying the hook and leaving a
  wrapper chaining to itself. InstallGitHook and RemoveGitHook now take
  a cross-process flock in the git common dir (never the hooks dir,
  which can be worktree-resident). Regression test mutation-verified:
  fails on the unlocked code with the exact self-chain corruption.
- Bare 'entire' no longer treats an UNUSABLE global config as "tier says
  no": the gate reads the enabled bit itself — an unreadable settings
  file gets a stderr warning instead of a wizard that would pin the repo
  out of the tier, and a tier-enabled-but-excluded repo is not funneled
  into repo-level setup either.
- expandTilde accepts only filepath.IsAbs patterns: the leading-slash
  allowance was redundant on Unix and fail-open on Windows, where the
  MSYS spelling /c/code/** can never match a drive-rooted root.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+	}
+	return release, nil

The double `TrimRight` calls on lines 332-336 create a subtle ordering bug. When `path` ends with `/.git`, the first `TrimRight` strips the trailing slash (`/repo/.git` → `/repo/.git`), then `EqualFold` strips `.git` (`/repo/.git` → `/repo`), but the second `TrimRight` has nothing to strip. The real issue: if someone passes `/repo.git/` (note: repo name contains `.git` as part of its name, not as a suffix), the first `TrimRight` yields `/repo.git`, the suffix check fails (no `.git` at position that would make `suffix >= 0`), and the dangling slash survives into owner/repo splitting, causing a fail-open in `exclude_origins` matching. Move the second `TrimRight` inside the `if suffix >= 0` block so it only runs when `.git` was actually stripped.

**Verified good:**

- **The B-merge hazard I went looking for isn't there.** On split B the body lives in an unexported `installGitHooks` that `global_setup.go:88` calls directly, so a lock in the exported wrapper would have been bypassed on exactly the concurrent path. I ran `git merge-tree` on B×A without touching the repo: the lock lands *inside* `installGitHooks`. Fine as-is.
- **`root.go`** now reads the enabled bit itself, warns on an unreadable global file instead of running the wizard, and no longer pins the repo. **`expandTilde`** is `filepath.IsAbs`-only, which closes the MSYS `/c/code/**` fail-open. Both of my lows are properly addressed. Suites and lint clean at HEAD.

**One new finding — `01M0GF8SFNS5` (Medium):** the regression test guarding the high-severity fix misses the regression it guards. I mutation-tested it by deleting the lock block:

| | their test | mine |
|---|---|---|
| GOMAXPROCS=1 | caught 4/20 runs | 3/3 |
| GOMAXPROCS=2 | 9/20 | 5/5 |
| GOMAXPROCS=4 | 9/20 | 5/5 |

CI runs it once, so a regression that destroys user hooks would ship 55–80% of the time. Their 8 installers is past the peak — more goroutines make it *rarer*, since most racers then read after the winner's write and take the marker short-circuit. Four properties fix it (all measured): 4 installers, seed every `buildHookSpecs` entry, repeat rounds, and assert the installed hook *chains* to the backup — that last one is what catches the orphan interleaving their assertions structurally cannot see.

**I also dismissed `01M0G4X77C79`** (Medium, filed by someone else against the `TrimRight` pair). Its named input `/repo.git/` normalizes correctly, and the reasoning contradicts itself — it claims the suffix check fails for a string ending in `.git`, and claims a slash "survives" that the first `TrimRight` already removed. Verified all six shapes through `ParseURL`; every one yields `repo`.

Two smaller notes, not filed:
- `lockHookInstall` takes a `ctx` but calls the unbounded `flock.Acquire`, whose own docs point latency-critical hook paths at `AcquireContext`. Contention is short here so it's near-theoretical, but a canceled hook now blocks in the kernel.
- Bare `entire` in a globally-*excluded* repo now prints generic help rather than offering setup. That's deliberate per the commit message, but it's the one case where the user plausibly does want the wizard, and they get no hint about what state the repo is in.

My test is still uncommitted at `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks_concurrent_install_test.go` (I fixed its call sites for the merge's dropped `localDev` param — it was the only thing breaking the `strategy` test build in my worktree). Want me to push it to the branch, or leave it for Peyton to pull from the finding?

Trail 1012 finding, mutation-measured: the previous test (8 installers,
one seeded hook, one round) caught the missing lock in only 6/20 runs, so

the lock removed: 5/5 runs at GOMAXPROCS=1 and 4 (was 6/20); ~5s, no
flakes with the lock in place.

content.text:
One new commit, `0b22946b6`, and it closes the last finding properly. Verified with the same mutation test I used to fail the old version — delete the `lockHookInstall` block, then count detections:

| | old test | new test |
|---|---|---|
| GOMAXPROCS=1 | 4/20 runs | **5/5** |
| GOMAXPROCS=2 | 9/20 | **5/5** |
| GOMAXPROCS=4 | 9/20 | **5/5** |

All four properties landed: 4 installers, every `ManagedGitHookNames()` entry seeded, 60 fresh-repo rounds as subtests, and the chain assertion that catches the orphan interleaving the old assertions structurally couldn't see. Cost is 5.4s plain / 6.5s under `-race`, which is proportionate for a data-loss guard. Full `strategy` suite green (127s, most of it pre-existing), lint clean, worktree clean.

I deleted my own duplicate `hooks_concurrent_install_test.go` — their version now covers strictly more than mine did, and two 60-plus-round concurrency tests in one package is wasted CI time.

Trail #1012 has **no open findings**. Across the six passes, everything filed is now either fixed on this branch, verified as handled upstack in split B/C, or dismissed with evidence.

One nit I didn't file, since it's pre-existing rather than from this commit: `gitHookNames` (line 27) and `buildHookSpecs` (its own five `name:` literals) are two independent lists of the same five hooks, and the new test now depends on them agreeing. Add a hook to `buildHookSpecs` only and it gets installed but never raced by the test; add it to `gitHookNames` only and the test fails with a confusing "backup missing". Deriving the specs from `gitHookNames` would remove that coupling. Say the word and I'll file it or fix it.
